```{r setup}
# Every figure is drawn from the result tables at render time and every number in the
# text is an inline expression over the same tables (protocol v2, RR-10, 2026-09-09).
# pandoc's PowerPoint writer places a figure and a following paragraph on separate
# slides, so figure slides use a two-column layout: the statement of what the figure
# shows on the left, the figure on the right; the speaker notes hold the detail.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(knitr); library(ggplot2)})
root <- tryCatch(here::here(), error = function(e) normalizePath(file.path(getwd(), "..", "..")))
P2 <- file.path(root, "results", "tables", "protocol_v2")
CL <- file.path(root, "results", "tables", "cluster_level")
rd <- function(...) { f <- file.path(...); if (file.exists(f)) read.csv(f, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE) else NULL }
kb <- function(d, digits = 3, ...) knitr::kable(d, format = "pipe", digits = digits, row.names = FALSE, ...)
df <- function(...) data.frame(..., check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
f2 <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.finite(x), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d), "NA")
pc <- function(x, d = 0) ifelse(is.finite(x), paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "%"), "NA")
sgn <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.finite(x), paste0(ifelse(x >= 0, "+", ""), formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)), "NA")
get1 <- function(x) if (length(x) && is.finite(x[1])) x[1] else NA_real_

# mean over cells with a 95% interval across cells (normal approximation over the cell values)
cell_ci <- function(d, val, by) {
  d |> group_by(across(all_of(by))) |>
    summarise(n = sum(is.finite(.data[[val]])), est = mean(.data[[val]], na.rm = TRUE),
              se = sd(.data[[val]], na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(pmax(n, 1)), lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se,
              pos = sum(.data[[val]] > 0, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}
forest <- function(d, y, facet = NULL, null = 0, xlab = "Spearman (mean over cells, 95% interval)", base = 15, colour = NULL) {
  g <- ggplot(d, aes(x = est, y = .data[[y]])) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = null, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, colour = "grey35", orientation = "y")
  g <- if (is.null(colour)) g + geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#1f4e79") else g + geom_point(aes(colour = .data[[colour]]), size = 3)
  g <- g + labs(x = xlab, y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = base) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
  if (!is.null(facet)) g <- g + facet_wrap(as.formula(paste("~", facet)), scales = "free_x")
  g
}
tlab <- c(level = "Biomarker level", prev = "Prevalence")
olab <- c(child_vitA = "Child vitamin A", women_vitA = "Women's vitamin A", child_iron = "Child iron", women_iron = "Women's iron",
          women_folate = "Women's folate", women_b12 = "Women's B12", child_zinc = "Child zinc", women_zinc = "Women's zinc")
arm_label <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", spatial_plus_domain = "Spatial smoother + covariates", spatial = "Spatial smoother",
               domain_enet = "Elastic net, domain components", raw_enet = "Elastic net, all columns",
               region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean", null_train_mean = "Training mean")

MD  <- rd(root, "data", "covariates", "harmonized", "predictors_admin2_shared_metadata.csv")
BM  <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_summary.csv"); BC <- rd(P2, "benchmarks_v2_cells.csv")
A1  <- rd(P2, "admin1_transport.csv"); CS1 <- rd(P2, "climate_soil_admin1.csv"); ND <- rd(P2, "nested_domain_selection.csv"); NC <- rd(P2, "transport_null_calibration.csv")
WS  <- rd(P2, "weight_sources_cells.csv"); NT <- rd(P2, "nce_targeting_metrics.csv"); NTS <- rd(P2, "nce_targeting_summary.csv")
DA  <- rd(P2, "domain_ablation_loco.csv"); SA <- rd(P2, "source_ablation_loco.csv"); SAS <- rd(P2, "source_ablation_loco_summary.csv")
TC  <- rd(P2, "training_country_curve.csv"); TCS <- rd(P2, "training_curve_climate_soil.csv")
UR  <- rd(P2, "urbanicity_conditioning.csv"); VC <- rd(P2, "variance_components_ceiling.csv"); AR <- rd(P2, "anchor_and_rank.csv")
CV  <- rd(CL, "cluster_vs_district.csv"); MBG <- rd(CL, "mbg_comparison_cells.csv"); TCLU <- rd(CL, "targets_cluster.csv")
RC  <- rd(P2, "risk_category_accuracy.csv"); IL <- rd(P2, "individual_level_models.csv"); IO <- rd(P2, "iodine_in_country.csv")
IT  <- rd(P2, "index_importance_top.csv"); IP <- rd(P2, "index_importance_patterns.csv"); ID <- rd(P2, "index_importance_domains.csv")
TG  <- rd(P2, "targets_v2.csv"); SY <- rd(root, "metadata", "survey_years.csv"); NE <- rd(root, "results", "tables", "national_estimates_all.csv")
SLR <- rd(P2, "sl_rank_loss_scores.csv"); SLH <- rd(P2, "sl_domain_index_scores_hapc.csv"); LI <- rd(P2, "addon_lsms_flunet_infill.csv")
SIG <- rd(root, "results", "tables", "signal_probes", "p4_admin1_continuous_predictors.csv")

# ---- quantities used in the text -------------------------------------------------------
Q <- list()
bm <- function(est, tg, arm, col = "mean_spearman") if (is.null(BM)) NA_real_ else get1(BM[[col]][BM$estimand == est & BM$target == tg & BM$arm == arm])
Q$n_pred <- if (is.null(MD)) NA else nrow(MD); Q$n_dom <- if (is.null(MD)) NA else length(unique(MD$domain))
Q$n_cells <- if (is.null(TG)) NA else nrow(distinct(TG, country, outcome))
Q$n_districts <- if (is.null(TG)) NA else nrow(distinct(TG, country, Admin1, Admin2))
Q$n_clusters <- if (is.null(TCLU)) NA else nrow(distinct(TCLU, country, cluster))
Q$infill_index <- bm("infill", "level", "domain_index"); Q$infill_index_p <- bm("infill", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$infill_jk <- bm("infill", "level", "region_mean_jk"); Q$infill_jk_p <- bm("infill", "prev", "region_mean_jk")
Q$infill_sp <- bm("infill", "level", "spatial"); Q$infill_spd <- bm("infill", "level", "spatial_plus_domain")
Q$infill_enet <- bm("infill", "level", "domain_enet"); Q$infill_raw <- bm("infill", "level", "raw_enet")
Q$region_index <- bm("region", "level", "domain_index"); Q$region_index_p <- bm("region", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$region_sp <- bm("region", "level", "spatial"); Q$region_enet_p <- bm("region", "prev", "domain_enet"); Q$region_raw_p <- bm("region", "prev", "raw_enet")
Q$tr_index <- bm("country", "level", "domain_index"); Q$tr_index_p <- bm("country", "prev", "domain_index")
Q$tr_index_pos <- bm("country", "level", "domain_index", "cells_positive"); Q$tr_index_pos_p <- bm("country", "prev", "domain_index", "cells_positive")
Q$tr_enet <- bm("country", "level", "domain_enet"); Q$tr_enet_pos <- bm("country", "level", "domain_enet", "cells_positive")
Q$tr_cells <- bm("country", "level", "domain_index", "cells")
Q$tr_a1 <- if (is.null(A1)) NA else get1(mean(A1$spearman[A1$arm == "domain_index" & A1$target == "level"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$tr_a1_p <- if (is.null(A1)) NA else get1(mean(A1$spearman[A1$arm == "domain_index" & A1$target == "prev"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$tr_a1_pos <- if (is.null(A1)) NA else sum(A1$spearman[A1$arm == "domain_index" & A1$target == "level"] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
Q$cs_d <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else get1(mean(ND$spearman[ND$arm == "fixed_cs" & ND$target == "level"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$cs_d_pos <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else sum(ND$spearman[ND$arm == "fixed_cs" & ND$target == "level"] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
Q$cs_d_p <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else get1(mean(ND$spearman[ND$arm == "fixed_cs" & ND$target == "prev"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$cs_a1 <- if (is.null(CS1)) NA else get1(mean(CS1$spearman[CS1$set == "climate_soil" & CS1$target == "level"], na.rm = TRUE))
Q$cs_a1_pos <- if (is.null(CS1)) NA else sum(CS1$spearman[CS1$set == "climate_soil" & CS1$target == "level"] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
Q$nested_vs_full <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else { w <- ND |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% c("full", "nested")) |> select(outcome, heldout, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman); get1(median(w$nested - w$full, na.rm = TRUE)) }
Q$nested_better <- if (is.null(ND)) NA else { w <- ND |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% c("full", "nested")) |> select(outcome, heldout, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman); sum(w$nested > w$full, na.rm = TRUE) }
Q$null_d <- if (is.null(NC)) NA else get1(NC$null_mean_q95[NC$tier == "admin2"]); Q$null_a1 <- if (is.null(NC)) NA else get1(NC$null_mean_q95[NC$tier == "admin1"])
Q$null_pos95 <- if (is.null(NC)) NA else get1(NC$null_positive_q95[NC$tier == "admin2"])
# in-fill: index vs jackknifed regional mean, cells better (level)
if (!is.null(BC)) { w <- BC |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "level", arm %in% c("domain_index", "region_mean_jk", "spatial")) |> select(country, outcome, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman)
  Q$infill_beats_jk <- sum(w$domain_index > w$region_mean_jk, na.rm = TRUE); Q$infill_paired <- sum(is.finite(w$domain_index - w$region_mean_jk)); Q$infill_index_minus_sp <- get1(mean(w$domain_index - w$spatial, na.rm = TRUE)) }
# geostatistical comparator
if (!is.null(MBG)) { m <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "infill") |> group_by(target, arm) |> summarise(v = mean(rho_agg, na.rm = TRUE), w = mean(wmae_agg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  gm <- function(tg, a, col = "v") get1(m[[col]][m$target == tg & m$arm == a])
  Q$mbg_index <- gm("level", "domain_index"); Q$mbg_mbg <- gm("level", "mbg"); Q$mbg_dhs <- gm("level", "mbg_dhs"); Q$mbg_gp <- gm("level", "mbg_gp")
  Q$mbg_index_p <- gm("prev", "domain_index"); Q$mbg_mbg_p <- gm("prev", "mbg"); Q$mbg_w_index <- gm("prev", "domain_index", "w"); Q$mbg_w_mbg <- gm("prev", "mbg", "w")
  w2 <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "level", arm %in% c("domain_index", "mbg")) |> select(country, outcome, arm, rho_agg) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = rho_agg)
  Q$mbg_index_better <- sum(w2$domain_index > w2$mbg, na.rm = TRUE); Q$mbg_cells <- sum(is.finite(w2$domain_index - w2$mbg))
  mr <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "region", target == "level") |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(v = mean(rho_agg, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  Q$mbg_region_index <- get1(mr$v[mr$arm == "domain_index"]); Q$mbg_region_mbg <- get1(mr$v[mr$arm == "mbg"]) }
# weight sources: paired against the index
if (!is.null(WS)) { w <- WS |> filter(estimand == "country", target == "level") |> select(country, outcome, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman)
  pd <- function(a) c(d = get1(mean(w[[a]] - w$domain_index, na.rm = TRUE)), b = sum(w[[a]] > w$domain_index, na.rm = TRUE), n = sum(is.finite(w[[a]] - w$domain_index)))
  Q$ws_decor <- pd("index_decor"); Q$ws_sparse20 <- pd("sparse20"); Q$ws_soft1 <- pd("index_soft1"); Q$ws_enet <- pd("domain_enet"); Q$ws_ridge <- pd("ridge_min")
  wi <- WS |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "level") |> select(country, outcome, arm, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = spearman)
  pdi <- function(a) get1(mean(wi[[a]] - wi$domain_index, na.rm = TRUE))
  Q$wsi_ridge <- pdi("ridge_min"); Q$wsi_enet <- pdi("domain_enet"); Q$wsi_lasso <- pdi("lasso_min"); Q$wsi_decor <- pdi("index_decor"); Q$wsi_sparse20 <- pdi("sparse20"); Q$wsi_sparse5 <- pdi("sparse5")
  Q$ws_1se_scored <- if (!is.null(WS)) sum(is.finite(WS$spearman[WS$estimand == "country" & WS$target == "level" & WS$arm == "enet_1se"])) else NA }
# targeting
if (!is.null(NTS)) { nt <- NTS |> filter(estimand == "infill"); Q$cap_index <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "domain_index"]); Q$cap_jk <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "region_mean_jk"]); Q$cap_null <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "null_train_mean"]); Q$cap_oracle <- get1(nt$mean_capture[nt$arm == "oracle_ceiling"]) }
# ablation
abl_delta <- function(X, unit) {   # per cell: full-model Spearman (row "ALL") minus the value with the unit dropped
  full <- X |> filter(variant == "full", .data[[unit]] == "ALL") |> select(target, outcome, heldout, full = spearman)
  X |> filter(variant == "drop", .data[[unit]] != "ALL") |> inner_join(full, by = c("target", "outcome", "heldout")) |> mutate(delta = full - spearman)
}
if (!is.null(DA)) { das <- abl_delta(DA, "domain") |> filter(target == "level") |> group_by(domain) |> summarise(delta = mean(delta, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> arrange(desc(delta))
  Q$da_top <- head(das, 5); Q$da_neg <- sum(das$delta <= 0); Q$da_n <- nrow(das) }
if (!is.null(SA)) { sas <- abl_delta(SA, "source") |> filter(target == "level") |> group_by(source) |> summarise(full = mean(full, na.rm = TRUE), drop = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  Q$sa_dhs_full <- get1(sas$full[sas$source == "DHS"]); Q$sa_dhs_drop <- get1(sas$drop[sas$source == "DHS"]); Q$sa_dhs_cols <- if (is.null(SAS)) NA else get1(SAS$n_cols[SAS$source == "DHS" & SAS$target == "level"]) }
# training curve slope
if (!is.null(TC)) { tcm <- TC |> filter(arm == "domain_index", target == "level") |> group_by(n_train_countries) |> summarise(v = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$tc_slope <- get1((tcm$v[tcm$n_train_countries == 3] - tcm$v[tcm$n_train_countries == 1]) / 2) }
if (!is.null(TCS)) { tcc <- TCS |> filter(set == "climate_soil", target == "level"); Q$tcs_pos1 <- get1(mean(tcc$spearman[tcc$n_train_countries == 1] > 0, na.rm = TRUE)) }
# urbanicity
if (!is.null(UR)) { u <- UR |> filter(target == "level", tier == "admin2"); Q$ur_cs <- mean(u$rho_cs, na.rm = TRUE); Q$ur_partial <- mean(u$partial_cs, na.rm = TRUE); Q$ur_only <- mean(u$rho_urb_only, na.rm = TRUE) }
# ceiling
if (!is.null(VC)) { v <- VC |> filter(rung == "admin2", target == "prev"); Q$vc_honest <- mean(v$ceiling_vc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_split <- mean(v$ceiling_within_vc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_share <- mean(v$cluster_share_of_ceiling, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_at <- sum(v$achieved_spearman >= v$ceiling_vc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$vc_n <- sum(is.finite(v$ceiling_vc)) }
# survey design
if (!is.null(AR)) { a <- AR |> filter(rank_from == "prev", set == "climate_soil", fraction == 0.05) |> group_by(design) |> summarise(mae = median(mae, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  Q$ar_a1 <- get1(a$mae[a$design == "A1_anchor_rank"]); Q$ar_c <- get1(a$mae[a$design == "C_regional_survey"]); Q$ar_b <- get1(a$mae[a$design == "B_district_survey"])
  b <- AR |> filter(rank_from == "prev", set == "climate_soil", design == "B_district_survey") |> group_by(fraction) |> summarise(mae = median(mae, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$ar_b_match <- get1(min(b$fraction[b$mae <= Q$ar_a1])) }
# cluster track
if (!is.null(CV)) { cvm <- CV |> filter(set == "transportable", arm == "domain_index", estimand == "infill", target == "level"); Q$cv_agg <- mean(cvm$rho_agg, na.rm = TRUE); Q$cv_dist <- mean(cvm$rho_district_v2, na.rm = TRUE) }
# risk classes
if (!is.null(RC)) { r <- RC |> filter(scheme == "who_vitA") |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(ex = mean(exact_admin2, na.rm = TRUE), w1 = mean(within1_admin2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$rc_ex <- get1(r$ex[r$arm == "domain_index"]); Q$rc_w1 <- get1(r$w1[r$arm == "domain_index"]) }
# individual level
if (!is.null(IL)) { i <- IL |> group_by(set) |> summarise(auc = mean(auc, na.rm = TRUE), bs = mean(brier_skill, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$il_auc_s <- get1(i$auc[i$set == "survey_only"]); Q$il_auc_p <- get1(i$auc[i$set == "proxies_only"]); Q$il_auc_b <- get1(i$auc[i$set == "both"]); Q$il_bs_max <- max(i$bs, na.rm = TRUE); Q$il_cells <- sum(IL$set == "survey_only")
  ir <- IL |> filter(grepl("iron", outcome), set == "survey_only"); Q$il_iron_max <- max(ir$auc, na.rm = TRUE); Q$il_iron_min_top <- get1(sort(ir$auc, decreasing = TRUE)[3]) }
# SuperLearner comparisons (rank loss run: index, rank ensembles, random forest, mse ensembles)
if (!is.null(SLR)) { s <- SLR |> filter(arm %in% c("domain_index", "rank_nnls", "rf", "mse_nnls", "enet")) |> group_by(country, outcome, arm) |> summarise(sp = median(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = sp); s <- s[stats::complete.cases(s), ]   # the cells every arm scored
  sl <- function(a) get1(mean(s[[a]], na.rm = TRUE)); Q$sl_index <- sl("domain_index"); Q$sl_rank <- sl("rank_nnls"); Q$sl_rf <- sl("rf"); Q$sl_mse <- sl("mse_nnls"); Q$sl_enet <- sl("enet"); Q$sl_cells <- nrow(s) }
if (!is.null(SLH)) { s <- SLH |> group_by(country, outcome, arm) |> summarise(sp = median(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> group_by(arm) |> summarise(v = mean(sp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"); Q$sl_hapc <- get1(s$v[s$arm == "hapc"]) }
# importance shares
if (!is.null(ID)) { e <- ID |> filter(scope == "pooled", target == "level") |> group_by(outcome) |> summarise(env = sum(share[domain %in% c("Satellite embedding", "Climate and weather", "Soil characteristics")]), .groups = "drop"); Q$env_lo <- min(e$env); Q$env_hi <- max(e$env) }
if (!is.null(IT)) { ci20 <- IT |> filter(outcome == "child_iron", target == "level", rank <= 20); Q$ci_rep <- sum(ci20$incountry_sign_agree == ci20$incountry_fits); Q$ci_loco <- sum(ci20$loco_sign_agree == ci20$loco_fits) }
```

# Background

## Motivation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- Biomarker surveys are infrequent and costly, and programmes need sub-national estimates of vitamin and mineral deficiencies between surveys.
- This project predicts deficiency (iron, vitamin A, folate, B12, zinc) from proxies available across sub-Saharan Africa, using four biomarker surveys linked to `r Q$n_pred` district-level indicators.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](img/old_s02_intro_photo_1.png){width="4.2in"}
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Photo credit: Latter-day Saint Charities. GMS 2017 collaborators: University of Ghana, GroundWork, University of Wisconsin-Madison, KEMRI-Wellcome Trust; with UNICEF and Global Affairs Canada.
:::

## Aims

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="62%"}
- Sub-national deficiency estimates from proxies, validated against biomarker surveys.
- Identification of the districts at greatest risk, and a statement of which product survives validation: a ranking or a level.
- A statement of what a country without a survey can expect from the model, and what it must still measure.
:::
::: {.column width="38%"}
![](img/old_s03_goals_2.png){width="2.1in"}
:::
::::

# Data

## Surveys

```{r surveys}
dist <- if (!is.null(TG)) TG |> distinct(country, Admin1, Admin2) |> count(country) else NULL
clus <- if (!is.null(TCLU)) TCLU |> distinct(country, cluster) |> count(country) else NULL
oc <- if (!is.null(TG)) TG |> distinct(country, outcome) |> group_by(country) |> summarise(o = paste(sub("^(child|women)_", "", unique(outcome)) |> unique() |> sub(pattern = "vitA", replacement = "vitamin A"), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") else NULL
sy <- if (!is.null(SY)) SY |> filter(in_protocol %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE")) else NULL
if (!is.null(sy)) {
  d <- df(Survey = sy$survey, Fieldwork = paste(format(as.Date(sy$fieldwork_start), "%b %Y"), "to", format(as.Date(sy$fieldwork_end), "%b %Y")),
          Districts = if (is.null(dist)) NA else dist$n[match(sy$country, dist$country)], Clusters = if (is.null(clus)) NA else clus$n[match(sy$country, clus$country)],
          Outcomes = if (is.null(oc)) "" else oc$o[match(sy$country, oc$country)])
  kb(d, digits = 0)
}
```

::: {.notes}
`r Q$n_cells` country-outcome cells, `r Q$n_districts` surveyed districts, `r Q$n_clusters` survey clusters with GPS. Fieldwork dates were recovered for every cluster (Sierra Leone reconstructed from date of birth and age in days); ferritin, retinol and food prices are seasonal. Three surveys ran in the dry season and Malawi in the lean season. Likely question: why districts rather than regions. Districts are the programme unit; they sit below the surveys' design resolution, so the reliability ceiling slide reports what a perfect predictor could reach.
:::

## Outcomes

```{r outcomes}
kb(df(Outcome = c("Iron status", "Vitamin A status", "Folate", "Vitamin B12", "Zinc"),
  Population = c("Children 6 to 59 months; women 15 to 49 years", "Children 6 to 59 months; women 15 to 49 years", "Women 15 to 49 years", "Women 15 to 49 years", "Children; women"),
  Countries = c("All four", "All four", "Ghana, Sierra Leone, Malawi", "Ghana, Sierra Leone, Malawi", "Malawi only"),
  Biomarker = c("Serum ferritin, BRINDA-adjusted", "Retinol-binding protein, BRINDA-adjusted, retinol equivalent", "Serum folate", "Serum B12", "Serum zinc"),
  `Uniform cut-off` = c("< 12 / < 15 ug/L", "< 0.70 umol/L retinol equivalent", "< 10 nmol/L", "< 150 pmol/L", "IZiNCG, by time of draw")), digits = 0)
```

::: {.notes}
Two targets per cell: the deficiency prevalence, and the district mean of the negated log biomarker concentration (higher means worse), which carries more signal than the dichotomy and is reported alongside it. Vitamin A uses each survey's published RBP-to-retinol calibration before the 0.70 cut-off (VA-01). Iodine (The Gambia, Sierra Leone) is analysed within country only; a one- or two-country outcome has no cross-border test.
:::

## Conceptual framework: iron deficiency

![](img/old_s06_framework_1.png){width="8.6in"}

::: {.notes}
Adapted from Hess et al., Ann N Y Acad Sci 2023. The framework is unchanged; the ablation slides show which of its pathways the data can see.
:::

## Data assembly

- Clean and merge the national micronutrient surveys, with one uniform outcome definition per nutrient across countries.
- Link gridded layers to districts as zonal means, and to survey clusters as buffer means.
- Aggregate DHS and MICS indicators to districts with a cluster-level spatial model, so every district has a value.
- Rank-normalise every predictor within country before pooling, so that cross-country level offsets cannot act as signal.
- Reduce each of `r Q$n_dom` domains to its leading principal components; nothing is selected on the outcome.

## Predictors by source

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
`r Q$n_pred` predictors in `r Q$n_dom` domains. The household-survey aggregates and the Earth Engine layers are the largest blocks.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r sources, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.4, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(MD)) {
  s <- MD$source
  s <- dplyr::case_when(grepl("^DHS", s) ~ "DHS / MICS indicators", grepl("AlphaEarth", s) ~ "AlphaEarth satellite embedding", grepl("SoilGrids", s) ~ "SoilGrids / iSDA soil",
    grepl("^GEE", s) ~ "Earth Engine climate, land, built environment", grepl("IHME", s) ~ "IHME modelled surfaces", grepl("Malaria Atlas", s) ~ "Malaria Atlas Project",
    grepl("MapSPAM", s) ~ "MapSPAM crops", grepl("Koppen", s) ~ "Koppen / agro-ecological zones", grepl("WFP", s) ~ "WFP market prices", grepl("FAOSTAT", s) ~ "FAOSTAT (national)",
    grepl("Livestock", s) ~ "Gridded Livestock of the World", grepl("ESPEN", s) ~ "WHO ESPEN helminths", TRUE ~ "Other (WorldPop, GHS, RWI, water, HFID, GFDx)")
  d <- as.data.frame(table(s), stringsAsFactors = FALSE); names(d) <- c("Source", "n"); d$Source <- factor(d$Source, levels = d$Source[order(d$n)])
  ggplot(d, aes(n, Source)) + geom_col(fill = "#1f4e79", width = 0.7) + geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 4) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.28))) + labs(x = "Predictors", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The January deck listed LSMS (275) and FluNet (3) predictors; both are on disk but did not survive the all-country harmonisation and are scored as add-ons in the sensitivity section.
:::

## Predictor domains

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Columns per domain. The satellite embedding, child morbidity, climate and soil are the four largest domains; each enters the models as its leading principal components to 80% of variance.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r domains, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=5.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(MD)) {
  d <- as.data.frame(table(MD$domain), stringsAsFactors = FALSE); names(d) <- c("Domain", "n"); d$Domain <- factor(d$Domain, levels = d$Domain[order(d$n)])
  ggplot(d, aes(n, Domain)) + geom_col(fill = "#1f4e79", width = 0.7) + geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) + labs(x = "Columns", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
```
:::
::::

# Protocol

## Estimators

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
January: spatial ensemble learning

- SuperLearner library, weighted by cross-validated performance.
- Prescreening from thousands of predictors to 10 to 100 per model.
- Importance by change in mean squared error.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
Current: the corrected protocol

- Zero-tuning index: domain principal components weighted by their training-fold rank correlation with the outcome.
- SuperLearner retained as a comparison.
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
On the same folds the index scores `r f2(Q$sl_index)` against `r f2(Q$sl_rank)` for the rank-loss ensemble, `r f2(Q$sl_rf)` for random forest, `r f2(Q$sl_mse)` for the squared-error ensemble, `r f2(Q$sl_hapc)` for the principal-component highly adaptive ridge and `r f2(Q$sl_enet)` for the elastic net (mean of cell medians over the `r Q$sl_cells` cells every arm scored, prevalence, in-fill; SL-01 to SL-05, rerun on the RR-10 set). Likely question: why capacity hurts. With 14 to 87 districts per country the index has no tuned parameter, and every estimator that tunes one shrinks toward the constant under squared-error cross-validation; the weighting slide quantifies this over a family of penalties.
:::

## Estimands

```{r estimands}
kb(df(Estimand = c("In-fill", "Region extrapolation", "Country transport"),
  Question = c("Unsurveyed district in a surveyed region", "Whole unsurveyed region", "Country with no biomarker survey"),
  Folds = c("5-fold by district, 10 draws", "Leave-one-region-out", "Leave-one-country-out"),
  `Matched baseline` = c("Jackknifed regional mean; spatial smoother", "Spatial smoother", "Country-block permutation null")), digits = 0)
```

::: {.notes}
The earlier leaderboard scored transport-style models against an in-fill baseline that read the held-out district's own respondents; that comparison is withdrawn. Counts of positive cells have a fat null when a country's outcomes are correlated: with no transport at all, `r Q$null_pos95` of `r Q$tr_cells` cells are positive at the 95th percentile of the permutation null, so the mean rank correlation is the statistic compared with its null (`r f2(Q$null_d)` at district level, `r f2(Q$null_a1)` at regional level).
:::

# Results

## In-fill: district ranking accuracy

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Mean Spearman correlation over the scored cells with a 95% interval across cells. The index reaches `r f2(Q$infill_index)` on the biomarker level against `r f2(Q$infill_jk)` for the jackknifed regional mean (better in `r Q$infill_beats_jk` of `r Q$infill_paired` cells) and `r f2(Q$infill_sp)` for the covariate-free smoother.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r infill, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(BC)) {
  d <- BC |> filter(estimand == "infill", arm %in% names(arm_label)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("target", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(arm_label[arm], levels = rev(arm_label)), Target = tlab[target])
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Target", null = 0, base = 15)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Cells: `r Q$infill_paired` on the level (Sierra Leone's cells score NA at 14 districts). On prevalence the index scores `r f2(Q$infill_index_p)` against `r f2(Q$infill_jk_p)`. The smoother with covariates fitted to its residuals scores `r f2(Q$infill_spd)`; covariates add `r sgn(Q$infill_index_minus_sp)` over the smoother alone on the level. The penalised fits score `r f2(Q$infill_enet)` (domain components) and `r f2(Q$infill_raw)` (all columns). Likely question: why the smoother does so well. Inside a surveyed country the covariates mostly reproduce a smooth surface that neighbouring districts already provide; the value of the covariates is in unsurveyed regions and countries.
:::

## Region extrapolation

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Leave-one-region-out, mean over cells with a 95% interval. The index scores `r f2(Q$region_index)` on the level and `r f2(Q$region_index_p)` on prevalence; the penalised fits fall to `r f2(Q$region_enet_p)` and `r f2(Q$region_raw_p)` on prevalence.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r region, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(BC)) {
  d <- BC |> filter(estimand == "region", arm %in% names(arm_label)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("target", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(arm_label[arm], levels = rev(arm_label)), Target = tlab[target])
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Target", null = 0, base = 15)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Leaving out a whole region is where a smoother must extrapolate past the edge of its data. The index and the smoother stay close (`r f2(Q$region_index)` against `r f2(Q$region_sp)` on the level); the null training mean collapses. Ghana and Malawi are the countries where this estimand is well determined; The Gambia and Sierra Leone give one number per region.
:::

## Country transport

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Leave-one-country-out, `r Q$tr_cells` cells. The full index scores `r f2(Q$tr_index)` at district level (positive in `r Q$tr_index_pos` of `r Q$tr_cells`) and `r f2(Q$tr_a1)` at regional level; the climate-and-soil index scores `r f2(Q$cs_d)` and `r f2(Q$cs_a1)`. Dashed lines are the 95th percentile of the permutation null.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r transport, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(BC) && !is.null(A1) && !is.null(ND) && !is.null(CS1)) {
  d <- bind_rows(
    BC |> filter(estimand == "country", arm %in% c("domain_index", "domain_enet")) |> transmute(tier = "District", target, model = arm_label[arm], spearman),
    ND |> filter(arm == "fixed_cs") |> transmute(tier = "District", target, model = "Climate + soil index", spearman),
    A1 |> filter(arm == "domain_index") |> transmute(tier = "Regional", target, model = arm_label["domain_index"], spearman),
    CS1 |> filter(set == "climate_soil") |> transmute(tier = "Regional", target, model = "Climate + soil index", spearman)) |>
    cell_ci("spearman", c("tier", "target", "model")) |>
    mutate(Target = tlab[target], row = factor(paste(tier, model, sep = ": "), levels = rev(c("District: Zero-tuning domain index", "District: Elastic net, domain components", "District: Climate + soil index", "Regional: Zero-tuning domain index", "Regional: Climate + soil index"))))
  nulls <- df(tier = c("District", "Regional"), null = c(Q$null_d, Q$null_a1))
  ggplot(d, aes(est, row)) + geom_vline(data = nulls, aes(xintercept = null), linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, colour = "grey35", orientation = "y") + geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#1f4e79") +
    facet_wrap(~ Target) + labs(x = "Spearman in the held-out country (mean, 95% interval)", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Absolute levels do not transport: raw ferritin differs several-fold between surveys, so the transported product is a ranking. Prevalence: `r f2(Q$tr_index_p)` at district level (`r Q$tr_index_pos_p` of `r Q$tr_cells` positive) and `r f2(Q$tr_a1_p)` at regional level for the full index; `r f2(Q$cs_d_p)` at district level for climate and soil. The climate-and-soil pair was chosen on these four countries, so it enters the next country as a pre-registered prediction; honest nested selection of domains inside the training fold gives a median difference of `r sgn(Q$nested_vs_full)` from the full index (better in `r Q$nested_better` of `r Q$tr_cells`). Since 9 September the DHS-derived predictors are cluster-level spatial estimates at every district (DS-01), which changed nothing in-country and cost the full index 0.01 across borders. Likely question: what a correlation of `r f2(Q$tr_index)` means for a programme. The targeting slide answers in burden captured.
:::

## Geostatistical comparator

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
The DHS Program's model-based geostatistics fitted at the survey clusters (a spatial field plus covariates), scored on the same district folds. On the level it scores `r f2(Q$mbg_mbg)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_index)` for the index (index better in `r Q$mbg_index_better` of `r Q$mbg_cells` cells); on prevalence `r f2(Q$mbg_mbg_p)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_index_p)`.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r geostat, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(MBG)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", mbg = "Geostatistical, field + domain covariates", mbg_dhs = "Geostatistical, field + DHS covariate list", mbg_gp = "Geostatistical, field only", spatial = "Spatial smoother", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean")
  d <- MBG |> filter(estimand %in% c("infill", "region"), arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("rho_agg", c("estimand", "target", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), panel = paste(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region")[estimand], tlab[target], sep = ", "))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "panel", null = 0, base = 12, xlab = "Spearman across districts (mean, 95% interval)")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
INLA-SPDE Matern field with penalised-complexity priors, binomial on cluster counts for prevalence and Gaussian for the level, cluster predictions aggregated to districts by effective sample size; run with the first component of every covariate domain and with the DHS Program's ten-raster list (`r f2(Q$mbg_dhs)` on the level). The field alone scores `r f2(Q$mbg_gp)`. The geostatistical model has the lower absolute error on prevalence (`r f2(Q$mbg_w_mbg, 1)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_w_index, 1)` percentage points) because it estimates a level and shrinks toward it. Under region extrapolation the index scores `r f2(Q$mbg_region_index)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_region_mbg)`. The method needs measured clusters inside the country it predicts, so it has no country-transport estimand. Likely question: whether the two are complementary. Yes: the geostatistical model for a calibrated prevalence where a survey exists, the index for a ranking where none does.
:::

## Weighting of the domain components

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Alternative weightings of the same components on the biomarker level. In-country every joint fit loses to the marginal-correlation weights (ridge `r sgn(Q$wsi_ridge)`, elastic net `r sgn(Q$wsi_enet)`, lasso `r sgn(Q$wsi_lasso)`). Across borders the decorrelated index gains `r sgn(Q$ws_decor["d"], 3)` (better in `r Q$ws_decor["b"]` of `r Q$ws_decor["n"]`).
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r weights, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=5.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(WS)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Production index (pooled rank correlation)", index_soft1 = "Soft threshold, |z| < 1 to zero", index_decor = "Decorrelated across domains",
           index_meta = "Replication-weighted (meta z)", ridge_min = "Ridge, inner CV", ridge_nested = "Ridge, nested block CV on rank",
           domain_enet = "Elastic net, inner CV", enet_1se = "Elastic net, one-SE rule", lasso_min = "Lasso, inner CV", sparse20 = "Top 20 predictors, equal weights")
  d <- WS |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("estimand", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), Estimand = factor(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region", country = "Transport")[estimand], levels = c("In-fill", "Region", "Transport")))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Estimand", null = 0, base = 12)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The production weights are the infinite-penalty limit of a ridge regression on the components, so the rows are points along that family plus other sources of evidence for the weights (soft thresholding, meta-analytic replication across training countries, decorrelation across domains). Same folds and cells as every other arm; five in-fill draws. The one-SE rules return the null model in some cells (`r Q$ws_1se_scored` of `r Q$tr_cells` transport cells scored for the elastic net). The twenty-predictor composite gains `r sgn(Q$ws_sparse20["d"], 3)` across borders (better in `r Q$ws_sparse20["b"]` of `r Q$ws_sparse20["n"]`) and costs `r sgn(Q$wsi_sparse20)` in-fill. The soft threshold gained 0.02 across borders on the direct DHS estimates and `r sgn(Q$ws_soft1["d"], 3)` on the smoothed ones, so that gain was a property of noisy inputs. Both gains were found among 21 arms on these cells and are pre-registered for the next country rather than adopted. Prevalence-target version in the appendix.
:::

## Predictor weights by outcome

![](../../results/figures/protocol_v2/index_importance_top10_level.png){width="100%"}

::: {.notes}
The index is linear in the rank-normalised predictors, so its component weights project back exactly onto the `r Q$n_pred` columns (scripts 57 and 58). Shown: the ten largest weights in the pooled four-country fit on the biomarker level, coloured by data source; a star marks a sign not reproduced in every country's own fit. No predictor carries more than 2% of the index's variance; the satellite embedding, climate and soil together carry `r pc(Q$env_lo)` to `r pc(Q$env_hi)` depending on the outcome. Likely question: whether these are causes. They are not; the weights say where deficiency is. Livestock density carrying a positive sign for iron and B12 is ecological: pastoral zones are the dry, poor zones in these countries.
:::

## Predictors recurring across outcomes

```{r importance-patterns}
if (!is.null(IP)) {
  d <- IP |> filter(target == "level", outcomes_in_top20 >= 3) |> arrange(desc(outcomes_in_top20), mean_rank) |> head(12) |>
    transmute(Predictor = column, Domain = domain, `Outcomes (top 20)` = outcomes_in_top20, Signs = signs, `Mean rank` = mean_rank)
  kb(d, digits = 1)
}
```

::: {.notes}
Predictors in the pooled top 20 of three or more of the six outcomes on the level target, with the sign in each. One gradient recurs: districts that are drier and grassier, less productive (lower net and gross primary productivity), more pastoral, poorer (less home ownership, fewer women in paid work, less schooling) and more stunted rank worse on every deficiency. Outcome-specific signals sit below it: haemoglobin C allele frequency and cattle for child iron, the modelled anaemia surfaces for women's iron, helminth treatment coverage and the drought index for folate, elevation and coast distance for B12.
:::

## Sparse composites

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Equal-weight composites of the top 5, 10 and 20 predictors, membership chosen inside each training fold by back-projected index weight. Twenty predictors cost `r sgn(Q$wsi_sparse20)` in-fill and gain `r sgn(Q$ws_sparse20["d"], 3)` across borders; five predictors cost `r sgn(Q$wsi_sparse5)` in-fill.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r sparse, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(WS)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Full index", sparse20 = "Top 20, equal weights", sparse10 = "Top 10, equal weights", sparse10w = "Top 10, index weights", sparse5 = "Top 5, equal weights")
  d <- WS |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("estimand", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), Estimand = factor(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region", country = "Transport")[estimand], levels = c("In-fill", "Region", "Transport")))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Estimand", null = 0, base = 13)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Dawes' improper linear model: direction from the training fold, equal weights, rescaled like the index; nothing is chosen on held-out districts. Weighting the ten by their index weights instead of equally changes nothing. The composite is a transport and communication tool: twenty public layers a ministry can compute. Likely question: which twenty. The next slide lists the child iron members.
:::

## Child iron composite

```{r sparse-members}
if (!is.null(IT) && !is.null(MD)) {
  d <- IT |> filter(outcome == "child_iron", target == "level", rank <= 20) |> arrange(rank) |> left_join(MD[, c("column", "source")], by = "column") |>
    transmute(rank, p = paste0(column, " (", ifelse(beta > 0, "+", "-"), ")"), src = sub(" [(].*$", "", source))
  kb(data.frame(Predictor = d$p[1:10], Source = d$src[1:10], `Predictor ` = d$p[11:20], `Source ` = d$src[11:20], check.names = FALSE), digits = 0)
}
```

::: {.notes}
The twenty columns the four-country fit would deploy for child iron, in order of weight, with the sign of the contribution (plus means more deficiency). `r Q$ci_loco` of the twenty keep their sign in every leave-one-country-out fit and `r Q$ci_rep` in every country's own independent fit. In the benchmark the membership is re-chosen inside each training fold; this is the version fitted on all four countries. The other outcomes' composites are in results/tables/protocol_v2/index_importance_top.csv.
:::

## Ghana: survey and held-out prediction

```{r ghana-maps, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.6, dpi=130}
ok <- FALSE
try({
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(sf))
  source(file.path(root, "R", "protocol_v2.R"))
  S  <- read.csv(file.path(root, "data", "covariates", "harmonized", "predictors_admin2_shared.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
  PREDS <- intersect(MD$column, names(S)); domain_of <- stats::setNames(MD$domain, MD$column)
  B <- readRDS(file.path(root, "dashboard", "data", "admin2_boundaries.rds"))[["ghana"]]
  maps <- list()
  for (on in c("child_vitA", "women_iron")) {
    t <- TG[TG$country == "Ghana" & TG$outcome == on & is.finite(TG$y_prev) & is.finite(TG$n_eff), ]
    m <- dplyr::inner_join(t, S[S$country == "Ghana", c("Admin1", "Admin2", PREDS)], by = c("Admin1", "Admin2"))
    Xr <- prep_predictors_v2(as.matrix(m[, PREDS])); Y <- .v2_logit(m$y_prev); aux <- list(Admin1 = m$Admin1, y_nat = Y)
    pred <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(m), 10)
    for (r in 1:10) { folds <- make_folds_v2("kfold_district", nrow(m), k = 5, rep_id = r)
      for (f in unique(folds)) { te <- which(folds == f); tr <- which(folds != f); D <- domain_representation_v2(Xr, domain_of, sign_rows = tr)
        pred[te, r] <- ARMS_V2[["domain_index"]](tr, te, Y, NULL, D, aux) } }
    m$pred <- .v2_expit(rowMeans(pred, na.rm = TRUE)); rho <- cor(m$y_prev, m$pred, method = "spearman")
    g <- dplyr::left_join(B, m[, c("Admin1", "Admin2", "y_prev", "pred")], by = c("Admin1", "Admin2"))
    lab <- if (on == "child_vitA") "Child vitamin A deficiency" else "Women's iron deficiency"
    p1 <- "Survey 2017"; p2 <- sprintf("Held-out index prediction (rho = %.2f)", rho)
    long <- rbind(data.frame(g[, c("Admin1", "Admin2")], value = g$y_prev, panel = p1), data.frame(g[, c("Admin1", "Admin2")], value = g$pred, panel = p2))
    long$panel <- factor(long$panel, levels = c(p1, p2))
    maps[[on]] <- ggplot(sf::st_as_sf(long)) + geom_sf(aes(fill = value), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.15) + facet_wrap(~ panel) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::percent, na.value = "grey92", name = NULL) + labs(title = lab) + theme_void(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "right", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  }
  print(patchwork::wrap_plots(maps, ncol = 2)); ok <- TRUE
}, silent = TRUE)
if (!ok) cat("Maps could not be rendered in this session; see the dashboard.")
```

::: {.notes}
Districts with survey data only (grey: no survey clusters). Each district's prediction is made with that district held out (5-fold, averaged over ten draws). The model orders districts; the survey's own estimate at a single-cluster district is itself noisy, which is what the reliability ceiling slide quantifies.
:::

## Targeting value

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Share of the national deficiency burden in the fifth of districts each method ranks worst, in-fill, mean over cells with a 95% interval. The index reaches `r pc(Q$cap_index)`, the jackknifed regional mean `r pc(Q$cap_jk)`, no information `r pc(Q$cap_null)` and perfect knowledge `r pc(Q$cap_oracle)`.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r burden, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(NT)) {
  lab <- c(oracle_ceiling = "Perfect knowledge", domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", spatial_plus_domain = "Spatial smoother + covariates", spatial = "Spatial smoother", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean", null_train_mean = "No information")
  d <- NT |> filter(estimand == "infill", arm %in% names(lab)) |> group_by(country, outcome, arm) |> summarise(v = mean(capture_top20, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    cell_ci("v", "arm") |> mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)))
  forest(d, "Model", null = 0.2, base = 14, xlab = "Burden in the worst-ranked fifth (mean, 95% interval)") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The dashed line is the share a random fifth of districts would capture. The margin over the survey's own regional averages is small per cell and concentrates where regions hold three to five districts. Under transport, burden captured is at chance: the transported product is an ordering, not a targeting gain. Likely question: why the ceiling is only `r pc(Q$cap_oracle)`. Burden is spread across districts; even the true worst fifth holds under half of it.
:::

## Domain ablation under transport

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Loss in transported Spearman (biomarker level, `r Q$tr_cells` cells) when each domain is dropped and the components rebuilt, mean over cells with a 95% interval. The load-bearing domains are `r paste(head(Q$da_top$domain, 3), collapse = ", ")`; `r Q$da_neg` of `r Q$da_n` domains cost nothing to remove or help.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r ablation, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=5.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(DA)) {
  d <- abl_delta(DA, "domain") |> filter(target == "level") |> cell_ci("delta", "domain") |> arrange(est) |> mutate(domain = factor(domain, levels = domain))
  forest(d, "domain", null = 0, base = 12, xlab = "Loss in transported Spearman when dropped (mean, 95% interval)")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Positive values mean the domain is load-bearing. The survey-derived domains (household assets, fertility, education, child morbidity, health access) sit at or below zero: removing them does not hurt a new country and in several cases helps. A fixed climate-and-soil index transports at `r f2(Q$cs_d)` at district level and `r f2(Q$cs_a1)` regionally against `r f2(Q$tr_index)` and `r f2(Q$tr_a1)` for the full vocabulary; it was found on the same four countries it is scored on and enters the next country as a pre-registered prediction.
:::

## Source ablation under transport

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
The same ablation by data source. Dropping all `r Q$sa_dhs_cols` DHS and MICS columns moves the transported Spearman from `r f2(Q$sa_dhs_full)` to `r f2(Q$sa_dhs_drop)`.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r sources-ablation, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.8, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(SA)) {
  d <- abl_delta(SA, "source") |> filter(target == "level", n_cols >= 4) |> mutate(source = sub(" [(;].*$", "", source)) |> cell_ci("delta", "source") |> arrange(est) |> mutate(source = factor(source, levels = source))
  forest(d, "source", null = 0, base = 13, xlab = "Loss in transported Spearman when dropped (mean, 95% interval)")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The January deck's data-source importance was one country's in-sample change in mean squared error; this scores transport to a held-out country. Soil, the modelled IHME surfaces, crops and livestock carry it. The household-survey aggregates fit the training countries and do not carry, and the DHS Program's own cluster-level estimator of those aggregates (DS-01) did not change that.
:::

## Transport by number of training countries

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Every subset of training countries scored on each held-out country. The full vocabulary gains about `r f2(Q$tc_slope)` per added training country on the level; the climate-and-soil index starts higher and is positive in `r pc(Q$tcs_pos1)` of single-country fits.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r curve, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.4, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(TC) && !is.null(TCS)) {
  d <- bind_rows(TC |> filter(arm == "domain_index") |> mutate(set = "Full vocabulary") |> select(target, set, n_train_countries, spearman),
                 TCS |> filter(set == "climate_soil") |> mutate(set = "Climate + soil") |> select(target, set, n_train_countries, spearman)) |>
    group_by(target, set, n_train_countries) |> summarise(mean_rho = mean(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), lo = quantile(spearman, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(spearman, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(target = tlab[target])
  ggplot(d, aes(n_train_countries, mean_rho, colour = set)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) + geom_point(size = 3) + geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.45) +
    facet_wrap(~ target) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Full vocabulary" = "#1f4e79", "Climate + soil" = "#b15928")) +
    labs(x = "Training countries", y = "Transported Spearman (mean, IQR)", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Bars are the interquartile range over fits. Likely question: whether four countries are enough. The curve has not flattened at three training countries, which is the argument for adding surveys to the panel rather than changing the estimator.
:::

## Urbanicity conditioning

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Transported Spearman of the climate-and-soil index at district level (`r f2(Q$ur_cs)`), the same after partialling out an urbanicity composite (`r f2(Q$ur_partial)`), and urbanicity alone (`r f2(Q$ur_only)`).
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r urban, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.0, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(UR)) {
  d <- UR |> filter(target == "level") |> transmute(tier = ifelse(tier == "admin1", "Regional", "District"), outcome, heldout, `Climate + soil index` = rho_cs, `Partialling out urbanicity` = partial_cs, `Urbanicity alone` = rho_urb_only) |>
    pivot_longer(c(`Climate + soil index`, `Partialling out urbanicity`, `Urbanicity alone`), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "v") |> cell_ci("v", c("tier", "quantity")) |>
    mutate(quantity = factor(quantity, levels = rev(c("Climate + soil index", "Partialling out urbanicity", "Urbanicity alone"))))
  forest(d, "quantity", facet = "tier", null = 0, base = 13)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Urbanicity composite: night lights, population density, built surface, urban land cover, travel time to health care. The replicated associations (legumes, cattle, soil chemistry, night-time temperature, all toward more deficiency) describe where subsistence agriculture is, so an urban-rural gradient was the rival explanation; partialling it out moves the transported correlation by less than 0.02 and urbanicity alone does not transport.
:::

## Replicated indicators

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Indicators whose district-level association with the outcome has the same sign in every country with the outcome, ranked by pooled meta-analytic z. Positive z means more deficiency.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r signal, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=5.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(SIG)) {
  d <- SIG[SIG$sign_agree >= SIG$k_countries & SIG$k_countries >= 3 & SIG$group %in% c("child_vitA", "child_iron", "women_iron", "women_vitA"), ]
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$group), function(g) head(g[order(-abs(g$meta_z)), ], 4)))
  d$Outcome <- olab[d$group]; d$Direction <- ifelse(d$mu > 0, "More deficiency", "Less deficiency")
  d$key <- factor(paste(d$predictor, d$group), levels = paste(d$predictor, d$group)[order(d$group, d$meta_z)])
  ggplot(d, aes(meta_z, key, colour = Direction)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") + geom_point(size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ Outcome, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) + scale_y_discrete(labels = function(k) sub(" [a-z_A-Z]+$", "", k)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("More deficiency" = "#b2182b", "Less deficiency" = "#2166ac")) +
    labs(x = "Pooled z (random-effects meta-analysis)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Legume cultivation and cattle ownership track more deficiency at district level, the reverse of the household-level dietary relationship, which is an ecological-fallacy signature: the replicated axis is rural subsistence agro-ecology, useful for deciding where to look and uninformative about what to change. No malaria burden indicator replicates; child wasting tracks women's vitamin A deficiency in all four countries. An earlier version of these slides had the signs inverted.
:::

## Reliability ceiling

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
The correlation a perfect predictor of the true district prevalence could reach, given the survey's sampling noise, by country. The honest ceiling averages `r f2(Q$vc_honest)` against a split-half ceiling of `r f2(Q$vc_split)`; the index reaches its ceiling in `r Q$vc_at` of `r Q$vc_n` cells.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r ceiling, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(VC)) {
  d <- VC |> filter(rung == "admin2", target == "prev") |> transmute(country, outcome, `Split-half ceiling` = ceiling_within_vc, `Honest ceiling` = ceiling_vc, `Achieved, in-fill` = achieved_spearman) |>
    pivot_longer(-c(country, outcome), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "v") |> group_by(country, quantity) |> summarise(v = mean(v, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(quantity = factor(quantity, levels = c("Split-half ceiling", "Honest ceiling", "Achieved, in-fill")), country = sub("SierraLeone", "Sierra Leone", country))
  ggplot(d, aes(v, country, colour = quantity, shape = quantity)) + geom_point(size = 3.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("Split-half ceiling" = "grey55", "Honest ceiling" = "#1f4e79", "Achieved, in-fill" = "#b15928")) +
    labs(x = "Spearman correlation (mean over outcomes)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
A respondent-in-cluster-in-district-in-region variance model reproduces the split-half ceiling when the cluster is counted as geography, then removes the cluster term: `r pc(Q$vc_share)` of the split-half ceiling was cluster effect. Child zinc has no district geography; what looked like geography was the cluster, and the time of the blood draw explains part of the cluster effect (ZN-02).
:::

## Survey design: district error

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Median district error in percentage points against the share of a full survey sampled, four designs, `r Q$tr_cells` cells. At 5% of the sample a national anchor plus the transported ranking gives `r f2(Q$ar_a1, 1)` points, a regional survey `r f2(Q$ar_c, 1)` and a district survey `r f2(Q$ar_b, 1)`.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r anchor, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.4, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(AR)) {
  lab <- c(A1_anchor_rank = "National anchor + ranking", A2_region_anchor_rank = "Regional anchors + ranking", B_district_survey = "District survey", C_regional_survey = "Regional survey")
  d <- AR |> filter(rank_from == "prev", set == "climate_soil", design %in% names(lab)) |> group_by(design, fraction) |>
    summarise(mae = median(mae, na.rm = TRUE), lo = quantile(mae, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(mae, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> mutate(Design = lab[design])
  ggplot(d, aes(fraction, mae, colour = Design)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 2.5) + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = "Share of the full survey sample", y = "Median district error (percentage points)", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "bottom") + guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
A district survey matches the anchored ranking's level error at about `r pc(Q$ar_b_match)` of the full sample. The ranking wins on level error only: a district survey of any size captures more burden, because burden sits in populous districts that surveys measure precisely. Fitted symmetrically on a reduced survey, the model's error degrades in step with the survey's, so the model improves the ordering at any sample size and does not reduce the sample a survey needs.
:::

# Sensitivity analyses

## Add-on predictor blocks

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Median change in Spearman when a block is added to the base vocabulary, in-fill and district transport on the biomarker level, scored under one harness with the same folds.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r addons, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.8, dpi=160}
tags <- c(food_tm = "Food prices, fieldwork-matched", climate_tm = "Temperature and rainfall, fieldwork-matched", alphaearth = "Satellite embedding as own domain",
          livestock = "Livestock density", water_distance = "Distance to water and coast", espen = "Helminth burden and control", ihme_raster = "IHME surfaces as zonal means",
          fe_clim_aw = "Engineered climatology", fe_terrain_aw = "Terrain", fe_soil_aw = "Soil bioavailability")
rows <- lapply(names(tags), function(t) { i <- rd(P2, paste0("addon_", t, "_infill.csv")); l <- rd(P2, paste0("addon_", t, "_loco.csv")); if (is.null(i) || is.null(l)) return(NULL)
  di <- i |> filter(target == "level") |> group_by(country, outcome) |> summarise(d = mean(spearman[set == "plus"], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(spearman[set == "base"], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  dl <- l |> filter(tier == "admin2", target == "level") |> group_by(heldout, outcome) |> summarise(d = mean(spearman[set == "plus"], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(spearman[set == "base"], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  bind_rows(df(Block = tags[[t]], Estimand = "In-fill", d = di$d), df(Block = tags[[t]], Estimand = "Transport", d = dl$d)) })
rows <- bind_rows(rows[!sapply(rows, is.null)])
if (nrow(rows)) {
  d <- rows |> group_by(Block, Estimand) |> summarise(est = median(d, na.rm = TRUE), lo = quantile(d, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(d, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  ord <- d |> filter(Estimand == "Transport") |> arrange(est); d$Block <- factor(d$Block, levels = ord$Block)
  ggplot(d, aes(est, Block)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, colour = "grey35", orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#1f4e79") + facet_wrap(~ Estimand) + labs(x = "Change in Spearman when the block is added (median, IQR over cells)", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Bars are the interquartile range over cells. No block moves in-fill or transport by more than 0.01 at the median: the vocabulary is saturated. The fieldwork-matched temperature columns are among the most consistently associated with deficiency in the marginal scan yet improve no fold, because a covariate defined by when the survey happened cannot rank districts that have not been surveyed. Found in passing and fixed: the price columns used 2021 as The Gambia's survey year (fieldwork was January to April 2018), and the satellite embedding had been filed under agriculture.
:::

## Cluster-level fitting

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
The same index fitted at the survey cluster and aggregated to districts, against the district fit, on the same cells. In-fill on the level: `r f2(Q$cv_agg)` cluster-fitted against `r f2(Q$cv_dist)` district-fitted.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r cluster, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(CV)) {
  d <- CV |> filter(set == "transportable", arm == "domain_index") |> transmute(estimand = c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region")[estimand], target = tlab[target], country, outcome, `Cluster-fitted, aggregated to districts` = rho_agg, `District-fitted` = rho_district_v2) |>
    pivot_longer(c(`Cluster-fitted, aggregated to districts`, `District-fitted`), names_to = "fit", values_to = "v") |> cell_ci("v", c("estimand", "target", "fit")) |>
    mutate(panel = paste(estimand, target, sep = ", "), fit = factor(fit, levels = rev(c("District-fitted", "Cluster-fitted, aggregated to districts"))))
  forest(d, "fit", facet = "panel", null = 0, base = 12)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
`r Q$n_clusters` clusters with GPS; covariates as 2 km (urban) and 5 km (rural) buffer means from rasters on disk; the same estimands with folds cut by district and region. Cluster-fitted models trail district-fitted ones on every estimand and for transport. A precision-weighted index and empirical-Bayes shrinkage of cluster outcomes recover a third to a half of the gap. A matched-vocabulary comparison attributes the remaining gap to the layers rather than the fitting unit. The cluster track is a sensitivity analysis until its vocabulary is matched layer for layer.
:::

## Risk-class accuracy

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Share of districts placed in the correct WHO vitamin A band (under 2%, 2 to 10, 10 to 20, 20 or more), and within one band, mean over the vitamin A cells. The index in-fill: `r pc(Q$rc_ex)` exact and `r pc(Q$rc_w1)` within one band.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r riskcat, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.4, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(RC)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning index, in-fill", spatial_plus_domain = "Smoother + covariates, in-fill", spatial = "Spatial smoother, in-fill", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean, in-fill",
           transport_anchored_full = "Transport, full index + national anchor", transport_anchored_climate_soil = "Transport, climate + soil + national anchor")
  d <- RC |> filter(scheme == "who_vitA", arm %in% names(lab)) |> transmute(country, outcome, arm, `Exact band` = exact_admin2, `Within one band` = within1_admin2) |>
    pivot_longer(c(`Exact band`, `Within one band`), names_to = "measure", values_to = "v") |> cell_ci("v", c("arm", "measure")) |> mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "measure", null = NA_real_, base = 12, xlab = "Share of districts (mean, 95% interval)") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Out-of-fold predictions averaged over ten draws; transport rows use the held-out country's own national prevalence as the anchor (AR-01 design), the only honest way to put a transported ranking on the prevalence scale. The January deck's child vitamin A cell was 44 and 75 percent (exact, within one) for the full model from the old leaderboard. For iron and the other outcomes only the 20 percent threshold has a WHO source; the two-class accuracies are in results/tables/protocol_v2/risk_category_accuracy_summary.csv.
:::

## LSMS and FluNet predictors

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Ghana in-fill on the biomarker level with the base vocabulary, the base plus the LSMS block, and the LSMS block alone, median over ten draws.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r lsms, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(LI)) {
  d <- LI |> filter(country == "Ghana", target == "level", set %in% c("base", "plus", "addon_only")) |> group_by(outcome, set) |> summarise(rho = median(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), lo = quantile(spearman, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(spearman, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(Outcome = olab[outcome], Set = factor(c(base = "Base vocabulary", plus = "Base + LSMS", addon_only = "LSMS alone")[set], levels = c("Base vocabulary", "Base + LSMS", "LSMS alone")))
  ggplot(d, aes(rho, Outcome, colour = Set)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, orientation = "y", position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Base vocabulary" = "#1f4e79", "Base + LSMS" = "#b15928", "LSMS alone" = "grey50")) +
    labs(x = "Spearman (median, IQR over draws)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
LSMS exists for Ghana alone (GLSS7): 134 region-level household expenditure and asset means, broadcast to districts through the 16-to-10 region crosswalk, so the block varies only across ten regions. It does not improve any Ghana cell beyond noise and cannot be scored across borders. FluNet reports for Ghana and Sierra Leone only and is a national weekly count, constant within a country; it contributes nothing by construction. Both are candidates only if collected sub-nationally in the next countries.
:::

## Individual-level models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Person-level SuperLearner under district-blocked folds, Brier skill over the national prevalence, by country and outcome. Mean AUC over `r Q$il_cells` cells: `r f2(Q$il_auc_s)` for survey variables, `r f2(Q$il_auc_p)` for district proxies, `r f2(Q$il_auc_b)` for both.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r individual, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(IL) && nrow(IL)) {
  d <- IL |> mutate(Outcome = olab[outcome], set = factor(c(survey_only = "Survey variables only", proxies_only = "District proxies only", both = "Both")[set], levels = c("Survey variables only", "District proxies only", "Both")), country = sub("SierraLeone", "Sierra Leone", country))
  ggplot(d, aes(x = 100 * brier_skill, y = Outcome, colour = set)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") + geom_point(size = 2.6, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
    facet_wrap(~ country, nrow = 1) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Survey variables only" = "#1f4e79", "District proxies only" = "#b15928", "Both" = "grey45")) +
    labs(x = "Brier skill over the national prevalence (%)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Library: mean, elastic net, random forest; survey weights; inner folds blocked by district; outer 5-fold by district so no district's respondents are split across training and test. Survey variables: up to 80 respondent columns with 70 percent coverage after removing biomarkers, adjustments, identifiers, weights, dates and locations. Proxies: the district's domain components joined to each respondent. Person-level skill exists for iron only (survey-variable AUC up to `r f2(Q$il_iron_max)` in Ghana and Malawi); vitamin A, folate and B12 show none. The January figure (Brier skill 20 to 60 percent) came from folds not blocked by district and a survey set that included biomarker-adjacent variables. Aggregating a person-level classifier biases area means, so this remains a sensitivity analysis. Rerun on the RR-10 set on 10 September.
:::

## National-level track

```{r national}
if (!is.null(NE)) { d <- NE |> filter(model_type == "binary", outcome %in% c("child_vitA", "women_vitA", "child_iron", "women_iron")) |> group_by(Outcome = olab[outcome]) |>
  summarise(Countries = dplyr::n(), `Observed (mean)` = mean(obs_prev), `Predicted (mean)` = mean(pred_prev), `Mean absolute error (pp)` = 100 * mean(abs_diff), .groups = "drop"); kb(d, digits = 2) }
```

::: {.notes}
The January deck's national-level track (WHO VMNIS and BRINDA outcomes, FAOSTAT and policy predictors) lives in a separate sub-pipeline last run in April 2026. It is not part of the current protocol and has not been re-audited; the table is its last output for the four survey countries. It is the only track with time series and fortification policy indicators and is a candidate for a rerun under the corrected protocol.
:::

## Iodine

```{r iodine}
if (!is.null(IO)) { d <- IO |> filter(analysis == "protocol") |> mutate(cell = paste0(ifelse(country == "Gambia", "Gambia ", "Sierra Leone "), ifelse(target == "p_low", "UIC < 100", "median UIC"), ", ", ifelse(estimand == "infill", "in-fill", "region")),
    Model = c(null_train_mean = "Training mean", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean", spatial = "Spatial smoother", domain_index = "Zero-tuning index", spatial_plus_domain = "Smoother + covariates")[arm]) |>
    select(Model, cell, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = spearman) |> mutate(across(-Model, ~ ifelse(is.finite(.x), sprintf("%.2f", .x), "-"))); kb(d, digits = 2) }
```

::: {.notes}
Urinary iodine is measured in The Gambia (continuous, with household salt iodine) and in Sierra Leone (six WHO categories, non-lactating women); it left the modelling outcomes because a one- or two-country outcome has no leave-one-country-out test. Targets: district prevalence of urinary iodine concentration below 100 micrograms per litre and, for The Gambia, the district median. In-fill needs at least 15 districts, so it runs for The Gambia only; leave-one-region-out runs in both. Whether district salt iodisation tracks district iodine status is in results/tables/protocol_v2/iodine_in_country.csv (rows analysis = descriptive).
:::

# Conclusions

## Conclusions

- In-fill: the index scores `r f2(Q$infill_index)` against `r f2(Q$infill_jk)` for the survey's own regional averages and `r f2(Q$infill_sp)` for a covariate-free smoother.
- Transport: rankings carry (`r f2(Q$tr_index)` at district level, `r f2(Q$cs_d)` from climate and soil alone, null `r f2(Q$null_d)`); levels do not.
- Survey-derived inputs help inside a country and hold a new country back; the cross-border model should lean on the environment.
- A national anchor puts levels on the ranking: district error `r f2(Q$ar_a1, 1)` points at 5% of a full sample, matched by a district survey at `r pc(Q$ar_b_match)`.

## What the models can and cannot do yet

- Rank districts in a surveyed country? Yes: `r f2(Q$infill_index)`, null `r f2(Q$null_d)`.
- Rank districts in a new country? Yes, less well: `r f2(Q$tr_index)` against `r f2(Q$null_d)`.
- Which predictors carry the signal? Satellite, climate and soil.
- Prevalence in a new country from the model alone? Not yet.
- Prevalence with one national anchor? Yes: `r f2(Q$ar_a1, 1)` points at a 5% sample.
- Replace biomarker surveys? No: the ceiling is the survey's.
- Guide where the next survey samples? In design, not piloted.

::: {.notes}
The checklist agreed at the 10 September check-in, one row per question. Sources: benchmarks_v2_summary.csv (in-fill and country transport, biomarker level), transport_null_calibration.csv (95th percentile of the permutation null), nested_domain_selection.csv (fixed climate-and-soil set), index_importance_domains.csv (pooled shares of the three remotely sensed domains), anchor_and_rank.csv (AR-01, 5% fraction, climate-and-soil set, ranks from prevalence), variance_components_ceiling.csv (prevalence, admin2). Levels do not transport because the surveys differ in year, season, team and calibration (fe_transport_level_offset); the anchor supplies the level the ranking lacks. Guiding the next survey is a design result on these four surveys, not a pilot.
:::

# Appendix

## Weighting of the domain components: prevalence

```{r weights-prev, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.0, dpi=140}
if (!is.null(WS)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Production index (pooled rank correlation)", index_soft1 = "Soft threshold, |z| < 1 to zero", index_decor = "Decorrelated across domains",
           index_meta = "Replication-weighted (meta z)", ridge_min = "Ridge, inner CV", ridge_nested = "Ridge, nested block CV on rank",
           domain_enet = "Elastic net, inner CV", enet_1se = "Elastic net, one-SE rule", lasso_min = "Lasso, inner CV", sparse20 = "Top 20 predictors, equal weights")
  d <- WS |> filter(target == "prev", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("estimand", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), Estimand = factor(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region", country = "Transport")[estimand], levels = c("In-fill", "Region", "Transport")))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Estimand", null = 0, base = 13)
}
```

::: {.notes}
Prevalence target, same arms and folds as the biomarker-level figure. Mean Spearman over cells with a 95% interval across cells.
:::

## Geostatistical comparator: absolute error

```{r geostat-wmae, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.6, dpi=140}
if (!is.null(MBG)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", mbg = "Geostatistical, field + domain covariates", mbg_dhs = "Geostatistical, field + DHS covariate list", mbg_gp = "Geostatistical, field only", spatial = "Spatial smoother", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean")
  d <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "prev", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("wmae_agg", "arm") |> mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)))
  forest(d, "Model", null = NA_real_, base = 14, xlab = "Weighted mean absolute error, percentage points (mean, 95% interval)")
}
```

::: {.notes}
In-fill, prevalence. The geostatistical model estimates a level and shrinks uncertain districts toward the mean, which lowers absolute error; the index ranks and is rescaled to the training outcome's spread, which does not. If the deliverable is a prevalence figure for a named district, the geostatistical model is the right tool; if it is a ranking, the index is.
:::
